mainTopic: Levels of holiness for synagogues, ספרי תורה and their money, leftover communal funds, and charity pledged in another town
overview: The amud opens by siding with רב פפי: a בית הכנסת may be turned into a בית המדרש, as רבי יהושע בן לוי rules. Next comes בר קפרא's explanation of the פסוק about the burning of ירושלים. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue whether 'every great house' means a place of תורה or a place of תפילה, and the גמרא works out that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who said תורה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and asks whether one may sell an old ספר תורה to buy a new one. Several proofs are tried: from the משנה itself, from ברייתות about wrapping cloths and stacking scrolls, from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and from רבי מאיר. Each proof is rejected, and the גמרא stresses how serious it is to sell a ספר תורה at all. רבא rules that leftover money from a collection is free to use, and he defends this ruling against אביי's challenge from a ברייתא about a stipulation by the seven town leaders. After explaining the word דוכסוסיא, the גמרא discusses charity pledged by visitors in another town. It ends with the story of רב הונא, whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Siding with רב פפי using רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says logic favors רב פפי, since רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a בית הכנסת may be turned into a בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to follow רב פפי, because רבי יהושע בן לוי said: a synagogue may be made into a study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is settling the argument between רב פפי (permitted) and רב פפא (forbidden) by bringing support for רב פפי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that you may raise something to a higher level of holiness, but you may not lower it. רבי יהושע בן לוי permits turning a בית הכנסת into a בית המדרש. That shows he treats the בית המדרש as holier, which is exactly רב פפי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him / in accordance with his view
Study hall, a place of תורה learning

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a בית מדרש has greater קדושה than a בית כנסת. So a בית כנסת may be converted into a בית מדרש, but not the reverse.

phrases.english: It stands to reason to follow Rav Pappi,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A synagogue —
it is permitted to make it into a study hall.
phrases.notes: Turning it into a study hall counts as raising its holiness, so it is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the earlier argument between רב פפי and רב פפא, which came on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפי's view that a בית הכנסת may become a בית המדרש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי

steps.title: Conclusion: the הלכה follows רב פפי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: learn from this that רב פפי is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שמע מינה' means the proof stands and nobody pushes it away. רב פפי's view becomes the accepted conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: A בית הכנסת may be turned into a בית המדרש, because a בית המדרש is holier. This follows רב פפי, supported by רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב פפי: a בית הכנסת may be converted into a בית המדרש.

steps.title: בר קפרא opens his explanation of a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא quotes the פסוק listing the buildings burned at the destruction of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: What does this פסוק mean: 'He burned the house of ה', the king's house, all the houses of ירושלים, and every great house he burned with fire'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. בר קפרא quotes a פסוק, and this sets up his explanation of each part of it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to repeat itself. 'All the houses of ירושלים' should already include 'every great house'. That extra phrase invites a דרשה about what 'great house' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or explained in a non-literal (homiletical) way
What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Bar Kappara expounded: What is the meaning of what is written:
"And he burned the house of the Lord,
and the king's house,
and all the houses of Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת כׇּל בֵּית גָּדוֹל שָׂרַף בָּאֵשׁ״.
phrases.english: and every great house he burned with fire."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלכים ב כה:ט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. It is linked to the previous one because it also deals with בית כנסת and בית מדרש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק will be explained phrase by phrase.

steps.title: Explaining the first three parts of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: 'House of ה'' is the בית המקדש, 'king's house' is the palaces, and 'houses of ירושלים' means ordinary houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'House of ה'': this is the בית המקדש. 'The king's house': these are the king's palaces. 'All the houses of ירושלים': exactly as it sounds.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא explains the first three phrases of the פסוק, one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three phrases are explained simply. That leaves 'every great house' as the only phrase that needs a deeper explanation, and the next step deals with it.

phrases.english: "The house of the Lord" — this is the Holy Temple.
"The king's house" — these are the king's palaces.
"And all the houses of Jerusalem" — as they sound (literally).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first three phrases refer to the בית המקדש, the royal palaces, and ordinary houses.

steps.title: Argument over the meaning of 'every great house'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue. One says it is a place where תורה is made great, and the other says a place where תפילה is made great.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every great house he burned with fire': רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One says it is a place where תורה is made great. The other says it is a place where תפילה is made great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about the last phrase of the פסוק. It does not yet say which אמורא holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that 'great house' means a holy place used for serving ה'. They argue over which kind: a בית המדרש (תורה) or a בית הכנסת (תפילה).

keyTerms.meaning: One said (the speaker is not named)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say who holds which view. 'חד אמר... וחד אמר' leaves it open on purpose, and step 7 will figure it out.

phrases.english: "And every great house he burned with fire" —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: מָקוֹם שֶׁמְּגַדְּלִין בּוֹ תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: one said: a place where Torah is made great (a study hall),

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: מָקוֹם שֶׁמְּגַדְּלִין בּוֹ תְּפִלָּה.
phrases.english: and one said: a place where prayer is made great (a synagogue).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last phrase of the פסוק, which needs a deeper reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Great house' means either a בית המדרש or a בית הכנסת, and this is disputed.

steps.title: The פסוק behind each side
steps.stepSummary: The תורה view relies on 'יגדיל תורה'. The תפילה view relies on 'the great things אלישע did', which he did through prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says תורה relies on the פסוק 'ה' wanted, for His righteousness, to make תורה great and glorious.' The one who says תפילה relies on 'Tell me the great things that אלישע did', and what אלישע did, he did through prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where each view gets the word 'great' from. Each side finds a פסוק that calls its activity 'great'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה view finds the word 'great' (יגדיל) used for תורה. The תפילה view finds 'great things' (הגדולות) used for אלישע's miracles. Since those miracles came through prayer (רחמי), prayer is called 'great'.

keyTerms.meaning: He will make תורה great and glorious

phrases.english: The one who said Torah — as it is written:
"The Lord was pleased, for His righteousness' sake,
to make Torah great and glorious."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ישעיהו מב:כא.

phrases.english: And the one who said prayer — as it is written:
"Tell me, please, the great things
that Elisha has done,"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלכים ב ח:ד.

phrases.english: and what Elisha did —
he did it through prayer.
phrases.notes: For example, bringing the boy back to life (מלכים ב ד).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources for both sides of the מחלוקת in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each side finds a פסוק calling its activity 'great': תורה from ישעיהו, תפילה from the story of אלישע.

steps.title: Working out that רבי יהושע בן לוי said 'תורה'
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהושע בן לוי lets a בית הכנסת become a בית המדרש, he must hold that the בית המדרש is the 'great house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who said 'a place where תורה is made great', because he said: a synagogue may be made into a study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question left open in step 5, which אמורא said which view. It does this by repeating רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Allowing a בית הכנסת to become a בית המדרש shows that רבי יהושע בן לוי sees the בית המדרש as holier. So it fits that he calls the בית המדרש the 'great house'. That means רבי יוחנן holds the תפילה view.
steps.confusionAlert: The same ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי appears twice here, but it does a different job each time. In step 1 it supports רב פפי. Here it identifies who holds which view in the מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Conclude that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר מָקוֹם שֶׁמְּגַדְּלִין בּוֹ תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: is the one who said: a place where Torah is made great,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: A synagogue may be made into a study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles which אמורא holds which view in the step 5 מחלוקת, using the ruling from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע בן לוי holds 'great house' means a place of תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling that a בית הכנסת may be converted into a בית המדרש

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the תורה view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: רבי יהושע בן לוי said תורה, so רבי יוחנן said תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof stands. Now each אמורא is matched to his view: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds תורה, and רבי יוחנן holds תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Every great house' is either a בית המדרש (רבי יהושע בן לוי) or a בית הכנסת (רבי יוחנן). רבי יהושע בן לוי is consistent: he treats the בית המדרש as holier everywhere.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the identification made in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that 'great house' means a place of תורה, and רבי יוחנן holds it means a place of תפילה.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: money from a sold ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if a ספר תורה was sold, the money may not buy lesser ספרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they sold a ספר תורה, they may not buy other holy books with the money, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that you may only move up in holiness, never down. A ספר תורה is holier than books of נביאים and כתובים. So money from a ספר תורה may not go down to buy them.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: scrolls of נביאים and כתובים, which are less holy
'Etc.' The quote of the משנה continues past this point

phrases.english: But if they sold a Torah scroll
they may not buy scrolls [of Prophets and Writings], etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מָכְרוּ תּוֹרָה לֹא יִקְחוּ סְפָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'great house' discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money from selling a ספר תורה may not be used to buy something less holy.

steps.title: May you sell an old ספר תורה to buy a new one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether selling an old ספר תורה to buy a new one is allowed, and gives a reason for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may you sell an old ספר תורה to buy a new one? Maybe it is forbidden, because the holiness is not being raised. Or maybe it is fine, because there is no higher level to raise it to anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question it does not yet know the answer to. Is it allowed to swap a ספר תורה for another ספר תורה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the rule only allows going up in holiness, and here nothing goes up, so it is forbidden. Side two: a ספר תורה is already the highest level, so 'going up' is impossible. Staying at the same level should then be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
Raises it up to a higher level of holiness
Or perhaps. Introduces the second side of the question
It is fine, it is allowed

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about selling an old Torah scroll
to buy a new one with it?
Since it is not being raised up, it is forbidden,
or perhaps:
since there is no other higher level to raise it to,
it is fine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's 'only go up' rule to ask about a case of staying at the same level.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is swapping one ספר תורה for another ספר תורה allowed, even though the holiness does not go up?

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's exact wording
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only forbids buying ספרים, so it seems to allow buying a ספר תורה with a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'If they sold a ספר תורה, they may not buy ספרים.' Only ספרים are forbidden. A ספר תורה bought with money from a ספר תורה is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only the lesser ספרים as forbidden. By leaving out a ספר תורה, it seems to say that buying a ספר תורה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a proof
But this. Introduces what we learn from the wording
A Torah scroll bought with money from a Torah scroll

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מָכְרוּ תּוֹרָה לֹא יִקְחוּ סְפָרִים.
phrases.english: But if they sold a Torah scroll, they may not buy scrolls.
It is scrolls [of Prophets and Writings] that are not allowed,
but a Torah scroll with money from a Torah scroll is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֲבָל מָכְרוּ תּוֹרָה לֹא יִקְחוּ סְפָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That swapping a ספר תורה for a ספר תורה is allowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What the משנה leaves out: it forbids only ספרים.

steps.title: Rejected: the משנה is about after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The משנה talks about a sale that already happened. The question is whether you may sell in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is about after the fact. Our question was about doing it from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'if they sold.' That means the sale already happened, and it tells us what to do with the money now. Our question is whether you may plan such a sale from the start. These are two different questions.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact. It already happened

steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say the משנה is wrong. It says the משנה is about a different stage: money that already exists, not a sale you are planning.

phrases.english: The Mishnah is about after the fact.
What we were asking about is from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof mixes up דיעבד, a sale already done, with לכתחילה, planning a sale.

steps.title: A new source: the ברייתא on wrapping cloths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a cloth may wrap something holier than what it was made for, but not something equal or lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: you may wrap a ספר תורה in cloths made for חומשים, and חומשים in cloths made for נביאים and כתובים. But you may not wrap נביאים and כתובים in cloths made for חומשים, or חומשים in cloths made for a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, a ברייתא about wrapping cloths. The next step will draw the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloth may only be moved up to wrap something holier. The holiness levels from top to bottom are: ספר תורה, then חומשים, then נביאים and כתובים.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrolls that each hold one of the five books of the Torah

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We may roll a Torah scroll in the wrappers of single-book scrolls,
and single-book scrolls in the wrappers of Prophets and Writings.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים בְּמִטְפְּחוֹת חוּמָּשִׁין,
phrases.english: But not Prophets and Writings in the wrappers of single-book scrolls,
and not single-book scrolls in the wrappers of a Torah scroll.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: גּוֹלְלִין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בְּמִטְפְּחוֹת חוּמָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: An answer to the question in step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about wrapping cloths for holy scrolls.

steps.title: The inference: no use at the same level
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows a ספר תורה to use cloths of חומשים, but not cloths of another ספר תורה. So a swap at the same level is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches: we wrap a ספר תורה in cloths of חומשים. Cloths of חומשים, yes. Cloths of another ספר תורה, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the proof. The ברייתא suggests that moving something at the same level of holiness is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא picked cloths of חומשים, which are lower, for wrapping a ספר תורה. That implies cloths of another ספר תורה, which is the same level, may not be used. The same should apply to selling one ספר תורה to buy another.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. Points to the part of the source that proves the point

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about cloths, not selling. The גמרא applies the same idea, that same-level swaps are not allowed, to selling a ספר תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof leans toward forbidding the sale of an old ספר תורה to buy a new one. The next step challenges it, and step 16 concludes that this ברייתא proves nothing.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
We may roll a Torah scroll in the wrappers of single-book scrolls,
wrappers of single-book scrolls, yes,
wrappers of a Torah scroll, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof from the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That swapping a ספר תורה for a ספר תורה is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What the ברייתא leaves out: it allows cloths of חומשים, not cloths of another ספר תורה.

steps.title: The end of the same ברייתא points the other way
steps.stepSummary: The ending of the cloths ברייתא suggests that a ספר תורה may be wrapped in another ספר תורה's cloths. This is the opposite of what Step 14 inferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last line: 'and not חומשים in the cloths of a ספר תורה.' That implies a ספר תורה in another ספר תורה's cloths is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 14. It shows that the end of the same ברייתא can be read to allow a swap between two scrolls of the same level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 the גמרא inferred from the first line that a ספר תורה may not use another ספר תורה's cloths. But the last line only forbids a lower item, חומשים, from using a ספר תורה's cloths. That suggests a ספר תורה using another ספר תורה's cloths, which is the same level, is allowed. The two inferences contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part (end clause) of a source
Scrolls containing a single book of the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is now proving that a swap IS allowed. It is only showing that this ברייתא can be read both ways, so it cannot prove anything.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
and not single-book scrolls in the cloths of a Torah scroll.
This implies: a Torah scroll in the cloths of another Torah scroll
phrases.notes: This is what we learn from the last part of the statement.

phrases.english: is fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the inference of Step 14 with an opposite inference from the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the cloths ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The beginning and end of the ברייתא give contradictory inferences about the same-level case.

steps.title: No proof can be drawn from this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Because the inferences contradict, the cloths ברייתא tells us nothing about the same-level case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this attempt. The ברייתא of the cloths does not answer our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning implies the same-level case is forbidden, and the end implies it is allowed. So the ברייתא was not written with the same-level case in mind. It only teaches its plain rules about higher and lower items. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing can be learned from it

phrases.english: Rather, from this source
nothing can be learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the contradiction in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The cloths ברייתא cannot decide whether a same-level swap is allowed.

steps.title: Proof from stacking scrolls on top of each other
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows placing one ספר תורה on top of another. This suggests that one ספר תורה may be used for another of the same level.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: You may place a ספר תורה on top of a ספר תורה, a ספר תורה on top of חומשים, and חומשים on top of נביאים and כתובים. But you may not place נביאים and כתובים on top of חומשים, and you may not place חומשים on top of a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer the question. This ברייתא is about which scrolls may be placed on top of which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly allows putting one ספר תורה on top of another, which is the same level. If one ספר תורה may serve another this way, then perhaps selling one ספר תורה to buy another is also allowed.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחִין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה עַל גַּבֵּי תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: One may place a Torah scroll on top of a Torah scroll,
and a Torah scroll on top of single-book scrolls,
and single-book scrolls on top of Prophets and Writings.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים עַל גַּבֵּי חוּמָּשִׁין,
phrases.english: But not Prophets and Writings on top of single-book scrolls,
and not single-book scrolls on top of a Torah scroll.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַנִּיחִין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה עַל גַּבֵּי תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the cloths proof fails, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That a same-level swap (selling one ספר תורה for another) is allowed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא permitting one ספר תורה to be placed on top of another

steps.title: Stacking is different because it cannot be avoided
steps.stepSummary: Placing scrolls on top of each other is allowed only because there is no other way to store them. It does not show that a voluntary swap is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are bringing a proof from placing? Placing is different, because there is no other way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from stacking. Stacking is a special case that cannot be avoided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scrolls in the ark must rest on one another; there is no choice. Selling a ספר תורה is a choice a person makes. So permission in a case with no choice tells us nothing about a case where a person has a choice.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible / there is no other way

phrases.english: Are you speaking about placing?
Placing is different, because there is no other way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 17.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Stacking is unavoidable, but selling is a free choice, so the cases are not comparable.

steps.title: Rolling a scroll shows the same idea
steps.stepSummary: Rolling up any ספר תורה puts one sheet on top of another. This is allowed only because it cannot be avoided, and stacking scrolls is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, how could we ever roll up a scroll? One sheet rests on top of another! Rather, since there is no other way, it is allowed. Here too, since there is no other way, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection from Step 18. It points to the everyday act of rolling a scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every rolled ספר תורה has parts of the text lying on top of other parts of equal holiness. No one forbids this, so clearly 'no other way' makes something allowed. Stacking scrolls in the ark works the same way, so it cannot be a proof about selling.
steps.whatToRemember: A case that cannot be avoided, like stacking or rolling scrolls, is allowed for that reason alone. It cannot prove that a voluntary same-level swap, like selling, is allowed.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
how could we roll up a scroll?
But one sheet rests on top of another!
Rather, since there is no other way, it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר — שְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: Here too, since there is no other way, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, מִיכְרָךְ הֵיכִי כָּרְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 18 with the example of rolling a scroll.
steps.raayaObject: That an unavoidable situation is permitted on its own terms
steps.raayaSupportSource: The universal practice of rolling a ספר תורה, sheet over sheet

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל states directly that one may not sell an old ספר תורה to buy a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן, who said in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: A person may not sell an old ספר תורה to buy a new one with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that speaks to our exact question. It says that selling an old ספר תורה to buy a new one is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier sources, this teaching is about our exact case: an old ספר תורה sold for a new one. It sides with the view from Step 10 that a swap at the same level is no going up in holiness, so it is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source that answers the question from Step 10 directly, rather than by inference.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה יָשָׁן
phrases.english: A person may not sell an old Torah scroll
to buy a new one with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stacking proof fails, a new and direct source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That selling an old ספר תורה to buy a new one is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל via רבי יוחנן and רבה בר בר חנה

steps.title: The ban on selling an old scroll is only about carelessness
steps.stepSummary: The proof from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is rejected. He forbids selling an old ספר תורה only because the seller might never actually buy the new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is because of carelessness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 20. It says the ban there has a practical reason, not a basic rule against swapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids selling an old ספר תורה because the person may sell it and never get around to buying a new one. So the ban protects against carelessness. It does not prove that swapping one ספר תורה for another is wrong in itself.

phrases.english: There — it is because of negligence.
phrases.notes: He might sell the old one and never buy the new one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not settle the basic question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His ban rests on a practical worry (carelessness), not on a rule against same-level swaps.

steps.title: Sharpening the question: the new scroll is already written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question to a case with no risk of carelessness: the new ספר תורה is already written and waiting to be bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we ask the question, we mean a case where the new scroll is already written and sitting ready to be paid for. What is the law then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates its question in a sharper form. This sets up the next proof attempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once carelessness is removed as a factor, only the core question remains. Is it allowed in principle to give up one ספר תורה for another of equal holiness? The question stays open for now.

keyTerms.meaning: When we are asking / what we mean is
It is sitting ready to be redeemed (paid for)

phrases.english: When we ask: for example, where it is already written
phrases.notes: The new ספר תורה is finished.

phrases.english: and it is waiting to be redeemed — what is the law?
phrases.notes: The money from the sale goes straight to buying it, so nothing can go wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן כְּגוֹן דִּכְתִיב וּמַנַּח לְאִיפְּרוֹקֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rejection in step 21 to define a cleaner version of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it allowed to sell an old ספר תורה when the new one is ready and the swap happens right away?

steps.title: Proof from רבי מאיר: a scroll may be sold to learn תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר allows selling a ספר תורה to pay for תורה learning or for marriage. The גמרא infers that exchanging תורה for תורה is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר, one may sell a ספר תורה only to learn תורה or to marry a woman. Learn from this that exchanging תורה for תורה is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer the question. It reasons that if a ספר תורה may be sold for תורה learning, it may surely be sold for another ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling a ספר תורה to pay for learning trades one form of תורה for another. If that trade is allowed, then trading an old ספר תורה for a new one should also be allowed.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
One may not sell a Torah scroll
except to study Torah or to marry a woman.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תּוֹרָה בְּתוֹרָה שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: Learn from this: Torah for Torah is fine.
phrases.notes: This is what the גמרא learns from רבי מאיר's words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question sharpened in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That one ספר תורה may be sold to buy another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר (quoted by רבי יוחנן) allows selling a ספר תורה to pay for Torah learning.

steps.title: Learning and marriage are special cases
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. תורה learning leads to keeping the מצוות, and marriage fulfills the purpose of Creation. These goals are uniquely important, so they do not show that a plain scroll-for-scroll swap is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps learning is different, because learning leads to action. A wife is also different, as it says: 'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in.' But תורה for תורה — no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי מאיר. It explains why learning and marriage may be exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's two allowances may exist only because these two goals are so important. Learning brings a person to do מצוות. Marriage and children fulfill the verse in ישעיה about the world being made to be lived in. A new ספר תורה has no such extra importance, so the question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: He formed it to be inhabited (ישעיה 45:18)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that a ספר תורה is worth less than learning or marriage. It is only saying that these two goals are special exceptions, so we cannot use them as a model for an ordinary swap.

phrases.english: Perhaps study is different,
for study leads to action.
A wife, too, is special:
"He created it not to be empty; He formed it to be inhabited,"
phrases.notes: Having a family fulfills the purpose of Creation.

phrases.english: but Torah for Torah — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא שָׁאנֵי תַּלְמוּד שֶׁהַתַּלְמוּד מֵבִיא לִידֵי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי מאיר does not extend to swapping one ספר תורה for another.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Learning and marriage are uniquely important goals, so they may be exceptions that cannot be generalized.

steps.title: A strong warning against selling a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one should not sell a ספר תורה even if he has no use for it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that even a starving person who sells a ספר תורה or his daughter will never see blessing from the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person should not sell a ספר תורה, even if he does not need it. Going further, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: even if he has nothing to eat and he sold a ספר תורה or his daughter, he will never see a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא that shows how seriously selling a ספר תורה is viewed. This closes the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part forbids selling a ספר תורה even when the owner does not use it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further: even real hunger does not make the sale successful, and no blessing will come from that money. He groups it with selling one's daughter as a maidservant, which shows how grave a step it is.
steps.whatToRemember: No source proved that one may sell an old ספר תורה to buy a new one. The section ends by stressing that selling a ספר תורה is treated very seriously.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person may not sell a Torah scroll

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לוֹ.
phrases.english: even though he does not need it.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Going further, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Even if he has nothing to eat
and he sold a Torah scroll or his daughter —
phrases.notes: Selling a daughter means selling her as a maidservant.

phrases.english: he never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן לֹא יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs fail, the גמרא cites a related ברייתא on how serious it is to sell a ספר תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not sell a ספר תורה, and even a starving person who does so sees no blessing from the money.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule about leftover money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about leftover funds. רבא says the restriction applies only to money left over from a sale, not to money left over from a collection.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And the same applies to their leftovers.' רבא said: This was taught only when they sold a holy item and money was left over. But if they collected money and some was left over, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about leftover money, and רבא explains which case it is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a town sells a holy item and buys something holier, the extra money still carries the holiness of the item that was sold, so it can only be used to go up in holiness. רבא says that collected money is different. The leftover part of a collection was never used for anything holy, so it never became holy and can be used for anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover funds, money remaining after the purchase
They sold a holy item and had money left over
They collected money and had some left over
They only taught this in the case of…, a formula that limits a rule

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sold' and 'collected' are the whole key to this section. Sold money comes from something already holy, so it carries holiness. Collected money is just people's donations. Only the part actually spent on the holy item becomes holy.

phrases.english: And the same applies to their leftover funds.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught this only where they sold a holy item and money was left over,
but if they collected money and some was left over, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The leftover part of a collection was never made holy

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּכְרוּ וְהוֹתִירוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: leftover funds from selling holy items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover money keeps its holiness only when it comes from a sale. Leftovers from a collection may be used for anything.

steps.title: אביי quotes a ברייתא about stipulations
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא saying that the leftover-money restriction applies only when no stipulation was made. With a stipulation, the money may be used even for a דוכסוסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: When was this said? When they did not make a stipulation. But if they made a stipulation, it is permitted even for a דוכסוסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a ברייתא as the opening of a challenge against רבא. This step sets up the source, and the next step explains why it contradicts רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a stipulation (תנאי) can free the leftover money for a fully non-holy use, called a דוכסוסיא. The גמרא explains this word in step 31. The question that follows is which kind of leftover money the ברייתא means: sold money or collected money.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a ברייתא or משנה
In what case is this said? This limits an earlier rule
They made a stipulation, a condition stated in advance
A non-holy town use. The גמרא defines the word in step 31

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
In what case was this said? When they did not make a stipulation,
but if they made a stipulation, it is permitted even for a dukhsusya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רבא's distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that leftovers from a collection are automatically permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא implies that leftovers become free only through a stipulation. The next step shows why this clashes with רבא.

steps.title: אביי shows the ברייתא must mean collected money
steps.stepSummary: A stipulation cannot remove holiness from sold money, so the ברייתא must be about collected money. That would mean collected leftovers need a stipulation, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say they sold and had money left over, what good does a stipulation do? Rather, it must be where they collected and had money left over. So the reason it is permitted is that they made a stipulation. If they did not, it would not be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now spells out his challenge. He proves the ברייתא must be talking about collected money, and then shows that this contradicts רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sold money is already holy, and a simple stipulation should not be able to remove that holiness. So the ברייתא cannot mean sold money and must mean collected money. But then the ברייתא says collected leftovers are permitted only with a stipulation, while רבא said they are permitted automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
If you say, which introduces a possible reading
What difference does it make? What does it accomplish?
The reason is because…, which implies that otherwise it would not be so

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say they sold and had money left over,
what good does it do if they made a stipulation?
phrases.notes: A stipulation should not remove existing holiness

phrases.english: Rather, it must be where they collected and had money left over.
So the reason it is permitted is that they made a stipulation,
which means that if they did not stipulate, it would not be permitted!
phrases.notes: This contradicts רבא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge by working out what the ברייתא implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that collected leftovers are permitted without any condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First, a stipulation cannot help sold money, so the ברייתא must mean collected money. Second, the ברייתא then says collected leftovers need a stipulation. That contradicts רבא.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא means sold money with a leaders' stipulation
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא really is about sold money. The stipulation it means is a formal one made by the seven town leaders in front of the townspeople, and that kind of stipulation does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is where they sold and had money left over. This is what the ברייתא means: When was this said? When the seven town leaders did not make a stipulation in front of the townspeople. But if the seven town leaders made a stipulation in front of the townspeople, it is permitted even for a דוכסוסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. He explains that the ברייתא is about sold money after all, and the stipulation it mentions is a special, official one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed a stipulation cannot help sold money. רבא answers that a formal stipulation by the seven town leaders (שבעה טובי העיר) in a public meeting has the authority to do so. Since the ברייתא is about sold money, it says nothing about collected money, and רבא's ruling that collected leftovers are automatically permitted still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. It keeps the original reading and answers the challenge
And this is what it means, a re-reading of the source
The seven leaders who manage the town's affairs
In the presence of the townspeople, at a public meeting

steps.whatToRemember: There are three cases. Collected leftovers are permitted with no stipulation at all. Sold leftovers stay holy and may only be used for something holier. Sold leftovers become fully free only if the seven town leaders made a stipulation in front of the townspeople.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how much power the town leaders acting with public backing have over communal holy property. That idea runs through the rest of this סוגיא.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where they sold and had money left over,
and this is what it means:
In what case was this said?
When the seven town leaders did not make a stipulation
in the presence of the townspeople,
but if the seven town leaders made a stipulation
in the presence of the townspeople,
then even for a dukhsusya it is also permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the kind of stipulation is defined more precisely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A stipulation cannot help sold money, so the ברייתא must be about collected money and contradicts רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about sold money, and a formal stipulation by the seven town leaders in front of the townspeople does free it. רבא's ruling on collected money stands.

steps.title: אביי asks what the word דוכסוסיא means
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks a scholar who used to recite ברייתות before רב ששת whether he heard from רב ששת what the word דוכסוסיא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to one of the Sages who used to recite the teachings in front of רב ששת: Did you ever hear from רב ששת what 'dukhsusya' means?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא in the last step allowed leftover money to be spent even on a דוכסוסיא, but nobody has said what that word means. אביי now asks someone who might know, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not try to guess the meaning. He goes to a person who regularly recited teachings in front of רב ששת, because that person probably heard רב ששת explain hard words. The question is about the meaning of one word, not about the law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word from the ברייתא. It is explained in the next step.
Someone who recites or arranges the ברייתות and teachings in front of a great teacher

phrases.english: Abaye said to one of the Sages

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה מְסַדַּר מַתְנְיָתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: who used to recite the teachings before Rav Sheshet:
Did you hear from Rav Sheshet
what 'dukhsusya' means?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word that appeared in the ברייתא quoted in step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דוכסוסיא

steps.title: The answer: it means the town horseman
steps.stepSummary: The scholar answers in the name of רב ששת that דוכסוסיא means the town horseman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב ששת said: It means the town horseman.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar answers אביי. רב ששת explained that a דוכסוסיא is the town's horseman, the rider who guarded the town and carried its messages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא makes sense. With a proper stipulation, leftover money can be used even for something ordinary and secular, like paying the town horseman. This shows how far a stipulation can go in releasing the money.

keyTerms.meaning: The town horseman, a rider who served as the town's guard and messenger

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Sheshet said:
the town horseman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 30
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דוכסוסיא is the town horseman

steps.title: Lesson: ask someone who is often with the great Sages
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from this episode that a young scholar who does not understand something should ask a person who spends a lot of time with the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, a young Torah scholar who heard something and does not know what it means should ask someone who is often in the presence of the Sages. It is impossible that such a person did not hear about it from some great man.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side comment. אביי turns what just happened to him into general advice for students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer to אביי's question came from someone who recited teachings before רב ששת, not from a book. אביי reasons that a person who is often around great teachers has almost certainly heard hard words explained. So when you are stuck, go to that kind of person.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, so we learn from this
Someone who is often found in front of the Sages
A great man, meaning a great Torah authority

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,
this young Torah scholar

phrases.aramaic: דִּשְׁמִעַ לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא וְלָא יָדַע פֵּירוּשַׁאּ,
phrases.english: who heard something and does not know its meaning,
should ask it of one who is frequently before the Sages,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out קמיה in round brackets; the corrected wording adds למאן in square brackets, meaning "of the one who."

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ מִן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה.
phrases.english: for it is impossible that he did not hear it from some great man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from the question and answer in steps 30-31
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who does not understand a teaching should ask a person who is often in the company of great Sages
steps.whatToRemember: דוכסוסיא means the town horseman. When you are unsure what something means, ask someone who regularly learns in front of great teachers.

steps.title: Charity pledged by a group of townspeople in another town
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי מאיר, rules that a group from one town who pledged צדקה in another town must hand it over there. When they go home they take it back and use it for their own town's poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר: If people from one town went to another town, and the charity collectors there made them pledge charity, they must give it. But when they come home, they bring the money back with them, and with it they support the poor of their own town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new rule about town charity funds. It deals with a group of people from one town who were asked to pledge צדקה while visiting another town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While they are visiting, the group must actually give the money so it does not look like they are backing out of a promise. But the money really belongs to their home town's fund, so they get it back when they leave. Then they use it for the poor of their own town.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of a town, here a whole group traveling together
They required them to pledge a sum for charity
The poor of their own town

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this money goes to the poor of the town they visited. They give it there for appearances, but they take it back home for their own poor.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Residents of a town who went to another town
and they made them pledge charity: they give it,
and when they come home, they bring it with them
and with it they support the poor of their own town.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about where charity funds belong
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group pledging צדקה in another town gives it there, then takes it back home for its own town's poor

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the rule and adds the case of one person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule about a group. It adds that an individual who pledged צדקה in another town gives it to the poor of that town.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: If people from one town went to another town and were made to pledge charity, they give it, and when they come home they bring it back with them. But if one person went to another town and was made to pledge charity, it should be given to the poor of that town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's rule. The ברייתא also teaches a different result for a single traveler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי מאיר's ruling about a group, so it serves as a proof. It adds a contrast. A group's money is treated as belonging to its own town, but one person's pledge stays in the town he visited and goes to its poor.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא, introducing support
An individual, one person traveling alone

steps.whatToRemember: A group that pledges צדקה in another town takes the money back for its own poor. An individual's pledge goes to the poor of the town he visited.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule depends on who is giving. A whole group's charity stays tied to its home town, while a single person's pledge belongs to the place where he made it.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
Residents of a town who went to another town
and they made them pledge charity: they give it,
and when they come home, they bring it with them.
But an individual who went to another town
and they made him pledge charity:
it should be given to the poor of that town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 33 with a ברייתא and adds the case of an individual
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling in the name of רבי מאיר about a group's charity pledge
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ruling, which adds that an individual's pledge goes to the poor of the town he visited

steps.title: Visitors come to רב הונא's fast and give צדקה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא declares a fast. רב חנה בר חנילאי and his whole town come to him, are assigned צדקה, and pay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא decreed a fast day. רב חנה בר חנילאי and all the people of his town came to him. They were assigned an amount of צדקה, and they gave it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests the rule just taught about a group giving צדקה in another town. This step is only the setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case from the previous steps: a group from one town pledges צדקה in a different town. So the rule of רבי מאיר and the ברייתא should apply to them. Keep that in mind for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They imposed on them (assigned them an amount)

phrases.english: Rav Huna decreed a fast day.
phrases.notes: Public fasts were a time when צדקה was collected.

phrases.aramaic: עָל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב חָנָה בַּר חֲנִילַאי
phrases.english: Rav Ḥana bar Ḥanilai came to him
and all the people of his town.
phrases.notes: They were a group from another town.

phrases.english: Charity was imposed upon them, and they gave it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case of the rule stated in Steps 33-34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup of the story: a visiting group gave צדקה in רב הונא's town.

steps.title: The visitors ask to take their צדקה home
steps.stepSummary: As they leave, the visitors ask רב הונא to return their צדקה so they can use it for the poor of their own town.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they wanted to go home, they said to him: 'Let the master give it back to us, and we will go and support the poor of our own town with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors ask for their money back. Their request is based on the rule that a group takes its צדקה home with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר in Step 33, a group that pledged in another town takes the money back when it leaves. So the visitors' request looks fully justified. The question now is whether רב הונא will agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master give it to us
The poor of our own town

phrases.english: When they wanted to go home,
they said to him:
May the master give it back to us
and we will go and support with it
the poor of our own town.
phrases.notes: This uses the wording of the rule in Step 33.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The visitors apply the rule of Step 33 to their own situation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב הונא will return the צדקה so they can use it for their own poor.

steps.title: רב הונא quotes a ברייתא that limits the rule
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers with a ברייתא that begins: 'When is this said? When there is no…'. This passage stops mid-sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'We learned in a ברייתא: When is this said? When there is not there…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא starts answering by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא says the rule about taking the money home only applies in a certain situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בַּמָּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים' signal a limit: the rule is true only in some cases. The sentence continues on the next amud and explains which case is the exception. This is how רב הונא will answer the visitors.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רב הונא is rejecting רבי מאיר's rule. He is pointing out that the rule has a limit. The rule itself stays in place, and the ending of the sentence comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to them: It was taught in a baraita:
In what case is this statement said?
phrases.notes: This is the usual way of starting to narrow down a rule.

phrases.english: When there is no…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ תְּנֵינָא בַּמָּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the visitors' request by limiting the rule they relied on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule of taking the צדקה home applies only in a limited case. The limiting condition continues on the next amud.
